> **Status:** v0.40.0 — Loop 15 - the HoH runtime, slice one. Build the outer runtime that spawns three isolated role sessions (planner, developer, QA), validates their deliverables against schemas with a capped retry whose exhaustion is a recorded failure, freezes the candidate ref before QA and refuses if the tree moves, refuses developer writes outside the plan's allowlist, and versions each loop in git with loop-<t>-<role> tags. No Jev, no model calls at the gates - the gates are stubbed, and the runtime is what enforces the seat separation that role files could only request. Brief: docs/loops/loop-15-brief.md. Sequenced ahead of Loop 14 by D-019-era ruling; Loop 14 is re-briefed, not deferred. Autonomy boundary ruled (D-019): autonomous inside a branch, Aaron at master. First loop where acceptance is written by a seat (Probe) that neither set the objective nor built the candidate.

(b) A FRESH PROFILE HAS NO SessionStart HOOK AT ALL, and both hooks in ~/.claude/settings.json hardcode absolute paths into C:/Users/melve/Projects/Self-Improving-Agent. If acquiring one means hand-editing settings.json with an absolute path into one person's home directory, core is installable BY AARON ON THIS MACHINE, which is the proxy the brief forbids.
- Gap G-031: THIS GAP CORRECTS T-151's CLOSE NOTE AT REV 32 AND CANNOT BE WRITTEN INTO IT - a close note is write-once, so a wrong one is uncorrectable in place and only a pointer like this one can reach a reader of it. TWO FINDINGS. (1) THE CORRECTION: T-151's close note said 'all 19 files in docs/loops/ are LF in the working tree' and concluded the session-63 line-endings watch-out was stale. The measurement was correct; THE SCOPE WAS NOT STATED, and it was one worktree. 'Line endings are MIXED in this repo' is indeed wrong as a general condition - 1 file of 21, in 1 worktree of 3 - but the operative advice, DETECT PER FILE IN ANY SCRIPTED EDIT AND READ THE FILE BACK, stands and must NOT be dropped as stale by the next /end. (2) THE REAL DEFECT: a working-tree copy can disagree with the repository on line endings while git reports clean, and no check sees it. .gitattributes normalises on commit, so git STORES docs/loops/sia-mailbox-decisions.md as LF and `git show HEAD:<path>` returns LF; because `text eol=lf` makes git compare NORMALISED content, a stale CRLF working copy also reads clean in `git status` and in every diff. The repository is correct, one working tree is stale, nothing in the normal workflow reports the difference, and it survives until something forces a re-checkout of that path. A scripted multi-line edit against that file would hit exactly the mismatch the watch-out warns about, ON A FILE GIT SWEARS IS FINE.
- Gap G-032: Seat role knowledge is now tracked but nothing reads it. .agents/roles/*.md carries how each seat works, and no hook, command or pipeline loads it: agent-identity.ts parses only the frontmatter of AGENT.local.md then AGENT.md for name/role/partner, and a grep across open-brain/src and .claude/commands for 'roles/' returns nothing. Tracking fixed durability; reachability is a separate problem and is still open.
- Gap G-033: A freshness check served through the MCP server cannot report that server's own staleness, because the check it needs is the code the stale server lacks. ob_sync run before /mcp reconnect returned 23 passed with no sign of module-boundary, gitnexus-index or build-freshness — not because they failed but because that server process predated v0.40.0. The same gate run from the CLI showed 26 passed with all three. A green ob_sync is therefore only as current as the server build serving it, and nothing in its output says which build that was.
- Gap G-034: build-freshness PASS means 'this build matches this checkout', NOT 'this build is current' — so a checkout parked on an old commit with a matching build is GREEN while serving stale code to every session on the machine. Measured 2026-09-19: the main tree at HEAD e65f251, build stamped e65f251, master a1ed790, ELEVEN COMMITS BEHIND, and build-freshness returns '[pass]: build matches HEAD e65f251'. That tree is what both SessionStart and SessionEnd hooks and the open-brain MCP server run from, in every project on this machine. TWO FURTHER FAULTS COMPOUND WITH IT, and they are distinct rather than restatements. (a) EXTENDS G-033: a check served through the MCP server cannot report that server's own staleness, because the code it needs is the code the stale server lacks. (b) THE TREE-AWARE MESSAGE MAKES IT WORSE: run through MCP against a linked worktree, build-freshness prints 'the hooks and MCP server run from the MAIN checkout's build and are unaffected by this one' — a reassurance ABOUT THE VERY PROCESS THAT PRODUCED IT, asserted rather than measured, and false at the time it was printed because the main build was eleven commits behind. The wording added on 2026-09-19 to make the message true per-checkout is what makes this instance misleading.
- Gap G-035: The record's objective goes stale when a loop closes, and nothing enforces updating it. Found by Aaron on 2026-09-19: both seats' /start greetings read 'Objective: Loop 13 ...' after Loop 13 had been closed, tagged, and given a close-out document. The greeting is CORRECT - state-render.ts renders state.objective.text faithfully. The record was wrong: three planner close-out writes (rev 32, 33, 36) and the developer's /end (rev 35) all landed without a set_objective. Both command files say to update it and both say it as a 'should' - end.md line 92 'if the current objective is done, note that the next session should pick a new one'; end.md line 128 'set_objective - only if the objective changed'; start.md line 143 'if the objective is complete, say so on the NEXT line'. Neither seat said so. A human noticed. An instruction that exists in two files and fires in neither is rule 4 exactly.
- Gap G-036: The mutual-exclusion rule over the record - 'no seat takes a revision while another seat holds an unclosed session' - deadlocks a three-seat loop, and its proposed mechanism inherits the deadlock. Found while fixing the stale objective on 2026-09-19: both Forge and Probe had open sessions, so the rule as stated forbade the planner from writing set_objective - a write the loop needed before it could start. The developer's specced mechanism, 'ob_state refuses a write when another seat's session is open and unclosed', would have refused it too. The rule was written for two seats that alternate; with three seats whose sessions are long-lived and overlapping, a planner that cannot write mid-loop cannot rule mid-loop.

## Decisions

- 2026-09-19 — The HoH loop is autonomous inside a branch; Aaron holds master until the shadow-gate count says otherwise — Ruled by Aaron in-session to the planner seat, by returning the planner's recommendation verbatim: 'autonomous inside a branch, you at master, with the runtime recording what it would have done at each merge so your disagreements become a count. The day that count is zero across loops with real defects in them, remove the gate on evidence.' THIS RESOLVES THE CONFLICT RECORDED IN docs/HOH-JEV.md §6.2 AND docs/loops/loop-15-brief.md §5.1: hoh_jev.md specified a loop that never blocks on a human, which was incompatible with 'Aaron merges, on his word', a rule that has held for every loop in this record. WHAT IS AUTONOMOUS: the plan gate, the developer done-gate, QA scoring, retry, and rollback — closed questions with criteria written in advance, run by the runtime without a human. WHAT IS NOT: the merge to master. The runtime stops at a candidate commit and never merges, pushes to master, or tags. WHY THE MERGE STAYS HUMAN, ON EVIDENCE RATHER THAN NERVES: every serious defect found recently passed the automated checks and was caught by a human question or a human-ordered real run — the retirements check green through five merged PRs then 115 findings in the main tree; build-freshness shipped with its author's tests green and wrong in two checkouts of three; the main tree fifteen commits stale and reporting pass. A gate is a calibrated judge of the evidence it is shown, and every one of those failures was in the evidence, not the judgement. TypeSafe's own words: typed output guarantees the interface, not truth. THE EXIT CRITERION IS MEASURABLE: the runtime records, at every merge decision, what it WOULD have done. Aaron still merges. Each time his decision differs from the runtime's is counted. When that count is zero across several loops that contained real defects, the human gate is redundant and is removed — on evidence. If it is not zero, the count is exactly what would have been lost. This is 'see it red before you trust it green' applied to the human gate itself. WHAT NO GATE REPLACES, stated so it is not quietly automated later: asking the question nobody wrote down. Jev answers questions it is asked; the observation that Loop 14 was briefed against a world that no longer existed came from a person noticing, not from a gate.
- 2026-09-17 — Loop 13's C4 closes as a recorded failure — Ruled by Aaron in-session to the planner seat (Atlas), 2026-09-17, in the words 'yes, Loop 13's C4 closes as a recorded failure'. C4 asked whether core installs and runs with Node and git alone, memory absent. It does NOT, and the reason is the finding: THE MACHINERY IS INSTALLABLE; THE INSTRUCTION IS NOT. Forge ran a real install - fresh clone, npm install --omit=optional, better-sqlite3 confirmed ABSENT before anything ran, env vars pointed at nonexistent paths - and everything mechanical passed: install, build, sync --check (21 passed, 4 skipped, the three memory checks SKIPPING WITH THE REASON rather than passing), open-brain start exit 0, cli-bootstrap.js exit 0 with project detected and agent identity read. server.js died correctly, because it IS the memory half. The loop fails at the instruction layer only. Aaron ruled ONLY that the command surface and hook installation are not Loop 13's work. He did NOT rule them as the next loop's subject; that is recorded as an open task with its derivation, not as a decision. A loop that ends in an honest no is not a failed loop, and the brief was written to make this outcome reportable: it either passes or it does not, and there is no partial credit to hide in.
- 2026-09-17 — Loop 13 is Idea B - the module boundary — Aaron ruled, against the alternative of G-026 (recall precision), which he had earlier pencilled in. The Planner argued for Idea B and not on the grounds that it was owed a turn: G-026's urgency is contingent on recall being USED, and three consecutive loops have now run with zero recalls, so tuning precision on a system nobody queries optimises a thing whose value is unestablished. Idea B - core installable with Node and git, memory an opt-in module - is the instrument for the question open since Loop 9: not 'does injection change behaviour', which Loop 10 answered, but 'does the memory half get used at all'. Idea B had been scheduled as Loop 7 and displaced four times, every time into a loop that had its own subject, by the sentence 'it fits cleanly with what we are already touching' - a sentence the Planner itself wrote about the lifecycle cut four hours before quoting the pattern back.
- 2026-09-17 — ADR-031 - a sign-off transfers across an amend only when the amend is provably disjoint — Refines 'a sign-off does not transfer across an amend', which made every post-QA prose fix cost a re-QA and therefore made the cheap path be not fixing prose, or amending quietly. New rule: it transfers when the amend is provably disjoint from what was signed, and PROVABLY MEANS A DIFF THE QA SEAT CAN RUN - in practice `git diff --stat <signed-sha> HEAD -- <executable paths>` handed over showing empty. Paired with the error-table admission rule: the table records a wrong claim that reached an artifact, a commit, a counterpart or Aaron; a near-miss caught in-process by its own author goes in a separate register as an instance of a named family, never numbered. THE DIVIDING LINE IS ESCAPE, NOT SEVERITY. Both rules exist to stop a correctness rule taxing the behaviour it wants - a rule that adds a row every time someone checks their own work makes checking your own work look like failure. Requested by the seat that stood to benefit from the looser rule, after noticing it had already drafted the entry before asking.
- 2026-09-17 — Forge may publish its own loop branches — Aaron, resolving an inconsistency the Planner surfaced rather than used: Loop 11's Developer pushed loop/11-instructions and opened PR #18 under what it believed were the same instructions, while Forge held a standing 'tag, never push'. One instruction, two readings, a whole loop apart. Forge pushes and opens the PR; the Planner tags the merge commit on master. Loop 12 cost a few hours of an unopened PR because Forge declined to publish on a peer's say-so and then declined again on a relay of Aaron's answer, confirming with Aaron directly instead. Recorded as the right price rather than an over-caution: a peer cannot extend reserved authority, and a relay of an answer is still the same channel.

## Architecture Overview

3-tier hub-and-spoke memory protocol:

| Tier | Location | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| **Global** | `~/Obsidian Vault/` + `CLAUDE.md` | Cross-project experiences, reusable skills, user preferences |
| **Domain** | Tagged experiences in vault | Stack-specific knowledge (Convex patterns, Stripe gotchas, etc.) |
| **Project** | `.agents/` in each repo | Project-specific context (PRD, tasks, session logs) |

## Search Architecture (v0.6.0)

| Store | Search type | Access |
|---|---|---|
| SQLite FTS5 (knowledge-v2.db) | Keyword + snippet | `kb_recall` via open-brain MCP |
| Obsidian (Summaries/) | Semantic embeddings | `smart-connections__lookup` |
| SQLite vec (knowledge.db) | Semantic vector | Disabled — v1 IDs stale, rebuild pending |

## Key Distinction

- **Self-Improving Agent** = the memory protocol (how knowledge flows across sessions)
- **AI-First Development Framework** = the project template (how projects are structured for AI agents)
- These are complementary layers distributed from this repo, but they are not the same thing

## Research Context (Session 8)

Gap analysis against next-gen frameworks (STEM Agent, Memory-as-a-Tool, Anthropic Harness, Karpathy autoresearch). Full details: `docs/gap-analysis-next-gen-frameworks.md`. Knowledge base entries: IDs 155-161.
